subject: Close Playbook: MAP milestones, ramp economics & usage definitions
messages:
From: Samantha King <samantha.king@acmeco.com>
To: Evelyn Hart <evelyn.hart@redwood.com>
Cc: Danielle Ortiz <dortiz@acmeco.com>
Date: 2026-07-01T09:12:00-07:00
Subject: MAP draft + timeline for evaluation (ACME)

Hi Evelyn,

Thanks again for the demo today — the product looked promising. Per our conversation, I attached a draft Mutual Action Plan (ACME_MAP_v1.pdf) with the evaluation milestones we discussed. High-level asks from my side: we need clarity on pricing during the eval (credits/discounts), an estimated post-eval committed run rate (so I can brief finance), and confirmation on how usage is defined (token vs. request vs. session).

Key dates in the draft:
- Week 1 (Jul 6): Integration & smoke tests
- Week 3 (Jul 20): Model quality eval & baseline prompts
- Week 6 (Aug 10): Performance acceptance and recommendation to pilot
- Week 12 (Sep 21): Production ramp to 50k requests/month (target)

Can you share a short proposal on the commercial mechanics tied to these milestones (pricing, ramp discounts, and any true-up cadence)? Also — ACME legal will want an initial economics-friendly clause for price protection during the pilot.

Attached: ACME_MAP_v1.pdf (MAP draft)

Thanks,
Samantha
Samantha King
Head of AI Programs, ACME Corp

From: Evelyn Hart <evelyn.hart@redwood.com>
To: Samantha King <samantha.king@acmeco.com>
Cc: Marcus Lin <marcus.lin@redwood.com>, Connor O'Brien <connor.obrien@redwood.com>
Date: 2026-07-01T12:30:00-07:00
Subject: Re: MAP draft + timeline for evaluation (ACME)

Samantha —

Appreciate the clear MAP. We've reviewed and sketched a close playbook that ties milestones to a staged economics package. Summary below; I attached a short redline doc (redlines_econ_clause.docx) with suggested contract language for true-ups and price protection.

High-level commercial proposal (eval -> pilot -> committed):
- Eval period (weeks 1–6): free compute credits covering up to 50k tokens/day; additional usage billed at a 50% discount vs list.
- Pilot ramp (weeks 6–12): volume-based discount schedule triggered by weekly rolling committed qps; example: 0–10k reqs/mo = 10% off list, 10–30k = 20%, >30k = 30%.
- Committed contract (post Sep 21): annual commit with quarterly true-ups. True-up cadence: quarterly lookback; overages billed at agreed committed rate; any under-usage credited toward next quarter (no cashbacks).

Price protection & usage definition suggestions (summary):
- Price protection: any list price increases during the first 12 months post-commit will not apply to ACME for services covered by the signed SOW.
- Usage definition: billable unit = inference request (API call) where a single request = one prompt + streaming response (counted as 1 request). Token accounting will be provided in billing exports; when customers request token-based pricing we can map tokens -> equivalent request tiers.

Open items for ACME legal we expect to see as redlines:
1) True-up floor/ceiling language — ACME suggested a hard cap on retrospective billing; we propose a 90-day refund window and a quarterly cap on retrospective adjustments.
2) Definition of "production" vs "eval" traffic — we need explicit markers to avoid accidental billed production during test runs.
3) Price protection period & portability — duration and whether protections apply if customer swaps model variants.

Next steps: Marcus will draft the short SOW section that maps the MAP milestones to the discount schedule and Connor will review the redline language for legal comfort. Can ACME confirm which account owner will sign the SOW and whether finance prefers quarterly or monthly true-ups?

Best,
Evelyn Hart
Enterprise Solutions — Redwood Inference

From: Samantha King <samantha.king@acmeco.com>
To: Evelyn Hart <evelyn.hart@redwood.com>
Cc: Danielle Ortiz <dortiz@acmeco.com>
Date: 2026-07-03T10:00:00-07:00
Subject: Re: MAP draft + timeline for evaluation (ACME)

Thanks Evelyn — this is helpful. A few clarifying questions from finance & legal: 

1) True-ups: ACME prefers a monthly reconciliation (quarterly makes planning harder), and we need an explicit upstream cap on retrospective charges (finance asks for a 30-day billing window for disputes). Can you take a stab at wording that limits retrospective billings to a single monthly billing cycle unless fraud is suspected?

2) Usage definition: Our engineering team will be doing many short automated calls during integration. We need a desktop definition so we don't accidentally step into billed "production" traffic. Can you add a short list of markers (API keys labeled as dev/test, IP allowlist, and a "test_mode" flag) that Redwood will honor as non-production for the eval period?

3) Price protection: We like the 12-month protection but request a carve-out allowing ACME to select alternate model variants at equal economics if Redwood decommissions a model.

4) Discounts: Can you share a worked example for month 3 and month 9 spend levels so our CFO can model cash flow? (e.g., month 3 = 120k reqs -> X effective $/req after discounts and credits).

We'll review Marcus/Connor's language once it's up. Danielle is our procurement lead and will handle the SOW signature loop.

Appreciate the quick turnaround — Samantha

From: Marcus Lin <marcus.lin@redwood.com>
To: Samantha King <samantha.king@redwood.com>, Evelyn Hart <evelyn.hart@redwood.com>
Cc: Connor O'Brien <connor.obrien@redwood.com>
Date: 2026-07-08T15:22:00-07:00
Subject: Re: MAP draft + timeline for evaluation (ACME)

Samantha —

Thanks for the specifics. I've attached an updated MAP + commercial appendix (Drive link in related_links) and captured the legal-safe wording below addressing your items 1–3. Connor also reviewed and gave a green note with an adjustment on the retrospective cap.

Proposed contract language (short excerpts for SOW/Schedule):
- Monthly reconciliation & retrospective cap: "Customer and Vendor will reconcile usage monthly. Retrospective charges that arise from reconciliation will be invoiced within 30 days of the reconciliation period and may not exceed the greater of (i) 125% of the invoiced estimate for that month or (ii) $10,000, except in cases of willful misuse or fraud."

- Eval traffic identification: "Requests made with keys explicitly labeled 'dev' or 'test', or requests originating from IP ranges provided in Appendix A, or requests indicating a 'test_mode=true' header will be treated as non-production for the duration of the Evaluation Period and will not be billed beyond the Eval Credits allowance. Parties will jointly maintain a list of active test keys."

- Price protection & model portability: "For 12 months following the Effective Date of the SOW, Vendor shall not increase list prices applicable to Services covered by the SOW. If a Vendor-deprecated model is required to be replaced, Vendor will offer alternative model variants at equivalent economics (list price +/- 5%), subject to technical compatibility; parties will agree on mapping within 30 days of deprecation notice."

Worked examples (simplified):
- Month 3: 120k requests. Eval credits cover first 50k tokens/day (~assuming 1.2M tokens month). Billable requests = 120k - credits equivalence -> effective billed requests = 60k. At pilot discounts (assume 20% tier), effective price = $0.004/req -> month cost = $240. (Detailed spreadsheet attached in Drive link.)
- Month 9: 450k requests. Committed discount tier (>30k) = 30% off list -> effective price $0.003/req -> month cost = $1,350.

Next actions:
- Evelyn: finalize SOW appendix with the MAP timeline and signatory block.
- Connor: incorporate the agreed contract excerpts into the term sheet (I attached redlines_econ_clause.docx).
- Samantha / Danielle: confirm whether ACME prefers monthly or quarterly invoicing (we propose monthly reconciliations with quarterly reporting) and confirm the signing authority name.

If we get agreement by next Wednesday (2026-07-15) we can route the DocuSign for signature the same week and hit the MAP timeline without delaying the integration start.

Regards,
Marcus Lin
Commercial Lead — Redwood Inference
Attachments: redlines_econ_clause.docx, MAP appendix (Drive link)
